1.Nf3 d5 2.g3 c6 3.Bg2 Nf6 4.O-O.strategy: Gets the king to safety and the rook off the corner before any central decision. White keeps every option for the pawn centre, and the bishop already aims at Black's queenside along the long diagonal, behind the f3 knight.

1.Nf3 d5 2.g3 c6 3.Bg2 Nf6 4.O-O Bg4.strategy: Develops the bishop on the diagonal that attacks the f3 knight, before an ...e6 can close it in. The knight guards d4 and e5, so Black pressures it at once. The bishop can trade itself for the knight, which gives White the bishop pair.

1.Nf3 d5 2.g3 c6 3.Bg2 Nf6 4.O-O Bf5.strategy: Develops the bishop outside the pawn chain on the other diagonal, where it controls e4 and so hinders White's natural e-pawn advance. The price is that the bishop on f5 can be harassed and Black has to watch its retreat.
